01.n: The silver and the gold stand first in the Hebrew, ahead of the verb, putting the payment itself in front. Our register renders this word 'silver'; the KJV's 'the money' later in the verse is this same word.

04.r: The king of Judah set on the throne by Pharaoh.
04.n: Gesenius: the name means 'whom Jehovah has set up'; the son of Josiah, king of Judah, previously called Eliakim, citing 2 Ki. 23:34.

05.r: The king of Egypt, Judah's overlord.
05.n: Gesenius: Pharaoh is a common title of the ancient kings of Egypt, sometimes with a particular name added, as at the end of this verse.

06.r: Turns to how he raised the payment.
06.n: The brief's lexicon gives two uses: 'surely' and, restricting, 'only, but, yet'. Here it is the second: he paid, but only by assessing the land.

07.r: The king had the land valued so each could be charged.
07.n: The brief's lexicon gives this form as 'to value, tax'; Gesenius gives the root sense as to arrange in order. Our register renders this verb, of a levy, 'assess'. The noun 'valuation' later in the verse is from the same root.

08.r: Marks 'the land' as what was assessed.
08.n: This small word marks a definite direct object and has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'the land'.

09.r: Judah, its land and so its people.

11.r: Marks 'the silver' as what was to be given.

13.r: Gives the ground of the levy: Pharaoh's word.

14.n: Literally 'on the mouth of Pharaoh': the mouth as the organ of speech, and so his spoken order.

16.r: Every man was charged on his own.
16.n: The word for 'man', used here, as often, to mean 'each'. It stands first, ahead of the verb.

17.r: Each paid in proportion to what he was valued at.
17.n: Our register renders this noun 'valuation'. The brief's lexicon gives 'order, row' and 'estimate, valuation'. The translations differ widely: 'taxation', 'value', 'ability', 'wealth'.

18.r: The king pressed the people for the payment.
18.n: Gesenius: to impel, to urge, to drive, and also to demand tribute, followed by two accusatives, one of the tribute and one of the people; here both are marked, 'the silver and the gold' and 'the people of the land'. Our register renders this verb 'press' and keeps 'exact', the KJV's word here, for the creditor's verb. Our English puts the people first, for the sake of English.

19.r: Marks 'the silver' as one object of 'pressed'.

20.r: What was pressed out of the people.
20.n: The 'for' in our English is supplied by English idiom: the Hebrew puts 'the silver' as a direct object of 'pressed'.

21.r: Joins the gold to the silver as a second object.
21.n: 'And' with the object marker; counted with 'and the gold'.

22.r: The gold pressed out with the silver.

23.r: Marks the people as the other object of 'pressed'.
23.n: The object marker; the translations render it 'of' or 'from'. Counted here with 'the people of'.

24.r: The ordinary men of Judah who bore the levy.

26.r: The silver and gold went on to Egypt.

28.n: Gesenius: Necho, king of Egypt, son of Psammetichus. The BSB gives the full name earlier in its sentence.

07.n: τιμογραφέω, plural in Swete's text, 'they assessed'. The word is built from τιμή, value, and γράφω, write: to register a value.

13.n: Swete's text has ἐπὶ twice here; the second, which the brief leaves without a dictionary form, looks like a doubled word.

14.n: στόμα, mouth: the Greek keeps the Hebrew 'on the mouth of Pharaoh'.

17.n: συντίμησις, a valuation or assessment, from the same family as the verb used for 'assessed'.

18.n: ἔδωκαν, 'they gave': the Greek has the people give, where the Hebrew has the king press them.

23.n: μετὰ, 'with': the Greek reads 'with the people of the land'.
